question: In accordance with Article 3 of Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, the Commission has set itself the objective of protecting the health of consumers from risks posed by food. According to the WHO, processed meat has been classified under IARC group 1, meaning that there is convincing evidence1 that it can cause cancer. What is more, it is apparent from Europe’s Beating Cancer Plan that measures aiming to prevent exposure to UV radiation – which the WHO also classifies under IARC group 1 – are being put on hold2. 1.
How is the Commission ensuring that EU consumers are adequately informed about and protected against the health risks stemming from a high consumption of processed meat?
Does the Commission plan to support or commission further scientific research on the health effects of meat consumption?

How does the Commission plan to better protect consumers against carcinogenic substances in products, in particular by means of improved labelling and risk warnings, and what view does it take of the state of affairs in cosmetics3, where potential risks could be completely avoided by providing the appropriate information?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (9.3.2026) EU legislation1 does not foresee labelling of health risks stemming from a high consumption of processed meat. Horizon Europe2 supports research on health impact of additives in food and beverage3. The Commission’s Scientific Advice Mechanism started working on ultra-processed foods4.
The Commission also provides funding opportunities to address research and innovation on the causes and prevention of cancer under the EU Cancer Mission5.

A carcinogenic, mutagenic or reprotoxic (CMR) substance may only be used in cosmetic products if it has been granted a derogation from the general ban after having been assessed by the Scientific Committee on Consumer Safety and found safe for use in cosmetic products. For CMR category 1 substances, additional derogation criteria must be fulfilled.

The derogation applies exclusively to the particular use and only up to very low concentrations in a final cosmetic product. Moreover, the Cosmetic Products Regulation6 requires cosmetic products containing CMR substances to carry specific precautionary statements.

open-calls/horizon-europe_en. 3 ADDITIVES, https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/864219; SugarBiomarker, https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101158398. and the Commission’s reply to E-004753/2025 https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/E-10-2025-004753-ASW_EN.html. 4 As called for in the Vision for Agriculture and Food, the Strategy for European Life Sciences and the EU cardiovascular health plan.
